small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_SP (e.g. 32, 64) and BLOCK_OC=64/128 to increase the GEMM N dimension; SP_FULL = BLOCK_SP*POOL*POOL=64 currently is small for tl.dot — try BLOCK_SP=32 (SP_FULL=128) or 64 (SP_FULL=256) with BLOCK_IC=64.
- Cache weights once across the IC loop per (kh,kw) by hoisting w_off computation; better, swap loop order to iterate IC outermost and (kh,kw) inside, accumulating into the same acc to reuse loaded x rows when possible. Also try num_stages=3 with BLOCK_IC=32 to overlap loads.
- Add a config tile that uses fp16/tf32 mma via `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` and remove the inner ic_mask (IC=64 is divisible by 32/64 so masks are unnecessary) to cut predication overhead.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col-GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, OutSpatial_tile) where OutSpatial_tile covers a contiguous block of conv outputs (e.g. 128). Iterate K = IC*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=32/64 in a single inner loop using tl.dot, instead of the current nested kh/kw/ic triple loop — this gives larger, more regular GEMM tiles and avoids the SP_FULL reshape gymnastics.
- Fuse pooling at the epilogue by having each program compute a POOL-aligned output tile (tile covers POOL*POOL conv outputs per pooled output), apply (sub1, tanh, sub2), then reduce within the tile before storing — avoids reshape and lets the tile shape be chosen for GEMM efficiency independently of pool stride.
- Consider channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the GEMM-K (IC) loads are contiguous across the K dimension; pre-permute weights to (OC, KH, KW, IC) once at init. This should significantly improve memory throughput on the 4090.
